result.title: RecurSciBench: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement in Data-Driven Scientific Research
result.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are advancing the automation of data-driven scientific research. Recent advances in recursive self-improvement (RSI) offer the potential for these agents to continuously improve through experience, but evaluating transfer across scientific tasks requires executable, scientifically verifiable tasks and independent assessment of self-improvement gains. We introduce RecurSciBench, a scalable benchmark for evaluating RSI in data-driven scientific research. Its RecurSciPipe framework automatically constructs scientific modeling and data analysis tasks from raw datasets, with execution-based verification and scientific validity checks. RecurSciBench spans four scientific domains, multiple data modalities, and varied scientific objectives. We evaluate four RSI systems by comparing their initial and evolved states on independent tasks after evolution on source tasks, covering within-type, cross-type, and cross-domain transfer. Experiments show that the benefits of self-improvement vary across agent systems and scientific domains. Positive overall gains can coexist with regressions on individual tasks. Experience can transfer across task types and benefit other domains even without measurable gains in the source domain.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RecurSciBench，用 RecurSciPipe 从原始数据集自动构造可执行、可科学验证的建模与分析任务，并在同类型、跨类型与跨域设置下比较四个 RSI 系统演化前后的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「经验演化是否带来真实增益、总体提升与单任务退化并存」的独立评测思路，可能可供核查 latent 推理循环中增益归因与负迁移问题；但对象为科学任务智能体，与视觉推理无直接关联。
